signed: Fintan and Liefe, Skehana Hill Farm

visit.ground: A little over 200 acres outside Freshford, farmed organically. Cattle on the lower half, sheep and horses further up, a few pigs, the polytunnel, and an orchard.

hero.alt: The market garden at Skehana Hill, brassicas and sunflowers under a grey August sky

film_intro: Filmed by Provenance on the farm.
story: Skehana Hill is a little over 200 acres outside Freshford, Co. Kilkenny, run by Fintan and his wife Liefe, who farm it organically. Darragh visited on a foggy August morning, with every animal on the farm out on the land.

The cattle are the first thing you notice. They live on natural pasture with room to roam, a mix of plants to graze and forage through, and the peace to get on with it. At the bottom of the farm, beside the river that runs into Freshford, the herd grazes a bog that holds all sorts of life, birds, bees and the plants that feed them, and that whole corner reads as a small conservation area that happens to have cows in it. Further up the fields, closer to the house, is an open, scenic stretch where the sheep and the horses are kept, along with any cattle that need recovery and space.

The polytunnel is one of the most impressive things on the farm. Out of a small space comes an amazing amount of healthy organic food, enough greens and vegetables to feed the town. And the orchard is the most special part of it: apple trees of many kinds, grown without pesticides or chemicals and in tune with everything around them, and so full of birds it could pass for a sanctuary.

Up towards the hill, the pigs and the sheep share the ground. The sheep had broken into the field we walked, a proper field with different grasses coming through it, and behind it a hazel wood, bordered by a planted woodland, where life flourishes. One sycamore stands alone in the field, the tree Fintan calls his favourite, and the sheep lie in under it. Beyond that it is trees and landscape as far as you can see. The pigs have a quiet spot of their own, a handful of them, fed on windfalls from the orchard and on the vegetables that will never make it to a shop. Every animal here eats well. The cattle are grass fed, and anything else that goes into an animal is local organic grain or the haylage cut off the farm's own fields.

There is a place on the farm for medicinal herbs, and below it the agroforestry, reached along an old road into Freshford that no longer exists, past the remnants of old walls and buildings. Native trees are going in among the grazing. It is a sanctuary of sorts, where a fox might cross in front of you, and there is no phone signal at all.

It is a beautiful place run by good people, in an old part of Ireland where the cinema still has its sign over the door and the church is the most important looking building in town. A part of Ireland that still feels like Ireland. Skehana Hill is the first Provenance Featured producer: the full filmed visit, the photographs, and this page.

products.name: Beef
products.note: Grass fed and grass finished on the land, not in a shed. A mix of breeds: Angus, Hereford and Shorthorn bulls on continental cross cows.

products.name: Lamb
products.note: Finished on grass as far as the year allows, with a little of the farm's own barley and wheat in the autumn.

products.name: Pork
products.note: Just a couple of pigs, on organic barley, wheat and peas and the orchard windfalls. Last winter's batch ran in the woods.

products.name: Organic vegetables
products.note: Beds and a polytunnel on a rotation: tomatoes, salads, three kales, purple sprouting broccoli, cauliflower, courgettes, pumpkins, alliums and roots, and the Jerusalem artichokes that come back every year whether they are wanted or not. In among them, the puffballs and earthworms that say the soil is alive. A corner for experiments: soybeans and sweet potato this year.
